description: Set off on a unique adventure through southern Peru. Start by exploring Arequipa, with its colonial architecture and views of El Misti volcano. Then travel to Chivay to take in the breathtaking scenery of the Colca Canyon and relax in its hot springs. Witness the thrilling flight of the condor in its natural habitat and wander through picturesque Andean villages. An itinerary packed with history, nature and culture that will stay with you long after you return home.

Day 1: Arrival in Arequipa, city tour and visit to the Santa Catalina Monastery.
Day 2: Drive to Chivay, visit to the Colca Canyon and the Salinas y Aguada Blanca National Reserve, hot springs and folk show.
Day 3: Condor flight at the Colca Canyon, tour of the valley villages and return to Arequipa.
Day 4: Breakfast in Arequipa and transfer to the airport for your return flight.

itinerary.title: Arrival in Arequipa – The captivating White City
itinerary.description:
Welcome to the cradle of Peru’s mestizo culture and colonial history. When you land in Arequipa, you’ll be greeted by the imposing silhouette of El Misti volcano, which seems to watch over the city from its privileged position. Once at the hotel, you’ll have time to relax and settle in.
In the afternoon, we dive into the soul of the city on an exclusive city tour. The Santa Catalina Monastery, built from white sillar (volcanic stone), is a hidden gem that holds 400 years of history and secrets. You’ll wander through its inner streets, some so beautiful they look like they’ve been lifted from a painting. The medieval feel, the peaceful atmosphere and the views over the city will take your breath away.
Arequipa’s buildings blend Spanish architecture and local styles perfectly, with a touch of magic only volcanic stone can provide. Get your camera ready—every corner tells a story.
🛏️ Overnight in Arequipa, where colonial charm meets modern life.

itinerary.title: Arequipa / Chivay – Heading into the Andes
itinerary.description:
Wake up to the serenity of the Andes and get ready for a day full of natural wonders.
We start the day with a traditional breakfast and head toward the Colca Canyon, one of the deepest canyons in the world. The drive is a feast for the eyes and a journey through high-altitude ecosystems and dreamlike landscapes: pre-Inca terraced fields, snow-capped volcanoes and the vast altiplano (high Andean plateau).
The Salinas y Aguada Blanca National Reserve will surprise you with its vicuñas and the flamingos that live on its salt lakes. The crisp morning air will refresh you with its purity and calm.
At the Volcanoes Viewpoint, you’ll feel small before the magnificence of the Andes, stretching out before you in overwhelming beauty. At more than 4,800 m (15,750 ft) above sea level, you’ll enjoy an impressive view of the Chachani, Misti and Pichu Pichu volcanoes.
When you arrive in Chivay, you’ll be welcomed by the warmth of its people. The afternoon is set aside to enjoy the La Calera hot springs or those at your hotel, whose mineral waters relax and revitalize you after a day full of adventure. That feeling of well-being is the perfect prelude to an evening of local cuisine and a folk show.
🛏️ Overnight in Chivay, where you can rest surrounded by the Andes in a peaceful, authentic setting.

itinerary.title: The condor flight – The majesty of the Colca Canyon
itinerary.description:
After a very early breakfast, this day is devoted to one of the most impressive moments of your trip: the flight of the condor. First thing in the morning, we head to the Cruz del Cóndor viewpoint, a unique spot where condors glide just a short distance away, displaying their majesty over the Colca Canyon. Watching this magnificent bird rise above the canyon with its wings outstretched is something you’ll never forget.
Throughout the day, we’ll visit some of the most picturesque villages in the Colca Valley, such as Maca and Yanque, where locals keep their traditions alive: women weavers, farmers
and artisans who carry on the knowledge inherited from their ancestors. The pre-Inca terraces and colonial churches will take you back in time, letting you feel history with every step.
We’ll stop at the Choquetico and Antahuilque viewpoints, which offer panoramic views of the valley and its terraces—a testament to the remarkable farming techniques of pre-Inca peoples.
At the end of the day, we return to Arequipa, full of stories and experiences that will stay with you forever.
🛏️ Last night in Arequipa, perfect for a relaxed dinner with the best views of the volcanoes.

itinerary.title: Farewell with a heart full of memories – Arequipa / Lima or your next destination
itinerary.description:
After a final breakfast in Arequipa, we accompany you to the airport for your return flight. But this isn’t goodbye—it’s “see you soon,” because the wonders of Arequipa and the Colca will always stay with you.

itinerary.title: Arrival in Arequipa + Colonial City Tour
itinerary.description:
When you arrive in Arequipa, the “White City,” our team will welcome you and take you to your hotel. In the afternoon, we’ll set off on a fascinating tour of Arequipa’s historic heart.
You’ll take home an unforgettable image as you explore the Santa Catalina Monastery, a true city within the city, with narrow lanes, courtyards and cells full of living history. Open to the public since 1970, this convent is an icon of colonial architecture in South America and a time capsule that takes you back to the 16th century.
Next, we’ll stroll through Arequipa’s historic center, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, where you’ll admire colonial churches built of white sillar, a volcanic stone that gives Arequipa its distinctive glow.

itinerary.title: Full-Day Colca Canyon Tour – Nature, condors and Andean villages
itinerary.description:
Very early departure (2:30–3:00 a.m.) toward one of the deepest canyons on the planet: the Colca Canyon. After an Andean breakfast in Chivay, we continue to the famous Cruz del Cóndor viewpoint, where the flight of the Andean condor will leave you speechless. These sacred birds, a symbol of the Peruvian Andes, soar over a chasm more than 3,000 m deep.
Along the way, you’ll visit picturesque Andean villages such as Yanque and Maca, full of history, color and tradition. We’ll see colonial churches and pre-Inca farming terraces and learn about the lives of local farmers, who still grow quinoa, corn and kiwicha (amaranth) using ancestral techniques.
After lunch, we head back to Arequipa with scenic stops:
Patapampa (4,800 m (15,750 ft) above sea level): the highest point of the route, with an impressive view of the Andes; Pampa Cañahuas National Reserve: where you’ll see vicuñas, alpacas, llamas and high-Andean birds in their natural habitat.
Arrival in Arequipa around 6:00 p.m. Free time and overnight in Arequipa.

faqs.question: Do I need to be in good physical shape for the Colca Canyon tour?
faqs.answer: The tour includes easy walks and visits to viewpoints, so you don’t need to be athletic. However, if you have any health concerns or difficulty moving at high altitude, we recommend checking with your doctor before the trip.

faqs.question: How do I acclimatize to the altitude in Arequipa and the Colca Canyon?
faqs.answer: Although Arequipa sits at about 2,300 m (7,550 ft) and the Colca Canyon route reaches up to 4,800 m (15,750 ft), the itinerary is designed to let you acclimatize gradually. There is also a stop in Chivay for an Andean breakfast and a rest before continuing.

faqs.question: Is the condor flight at the Cruz del Cóndor guaranteed?
faqs.answer: Seeing the condors in flight is very likely, but as they are wild animals, we can’t guarantee exactly when they’ll appear. Even so, the site is known for a high chance of seeing them in their natural habitat.

faqs.question: Is it safe to visit the highest points, such as Patapampa (4,800 m (15,750 ft))?

From historic Cusco, through the mystical Sacred Valley of the Incas, all the way to awe-inspiring Machu Picchu, this adventure immerses you in a world of ancient history, dazzling landscapes and vibrant culture. Discover the legacy of the Incas as you explore ruins, charming villages and natural wonders such as the Rainbow Mountain and Humantay Lake. itinerary.title: Welcome to Cusco + City Tour and Inca Ruins
itinerary.description:
When you arrive at Cusco airport, our team will greet you with a warm Andean welcome. A comfortable transfer will take you to your hotel in Cusco, where we recommend resting and enjoying a cup of coca tea—ideal for adjusting to the altitude (3,399 m (11,150 ft) above sea level) as you acclimatize to the heart of the Inca world.
In the afternoon, at approximately 12:30 p.m., we’ll pick you up from your hotel to begin our Cusco City Tour through the historic Imperial City, a true architectural gem where Inca culture and colonial heritage come together. We’ll visit the majestic Plaza de Armas, the city’s beating heart; Cusco Cathedral, an imposing Baroque building that safeguards colonial and Indigenous treasures; and the legendary Temple of the Sun, or Qoricancha, the main Inca ceremonial center, whose structures are still charged with mysticism and architectural precision.
Then we’ll head out to the ruins just outside Cusco to visit: Sacsayhuamán, a fortress of cyclopean stones fitted together without mortar with a precision that challenges modern engineering; Qenqo, a ceremonial center carved into the living rock; Tambomachay, known as the “Inca’s Bath,” dedicated to the worship of water; and Puca Pucara, a former military post that controlled and guarded access to the city.
In the evening, if you wish, you can join a Welcome Dinner (optional) at one of Cusco’s best restaurants, savoring the finest contemporary Andean cuisine.

itinerary.title: Sacred Valley + Train to Machu Picchu Pueblo
itinerary.description:
After breakfast, we’ll set off for the majestic Sacred Valley of the Incas, a place full of natural energy and ancient remains. Our first stop will be the charming town of Pisac, where its traditional craft market lets you discover colorful textiles, ceramics and Andean jewelry while you chat with locals who keep their traditions alive.
Next, we’ll travel through the fertile valleys of Calca and Urubamba, where we’ll stop for a delicious buffet lunch (included), featuring fresh regional produce and traditional dishes that capture the essence of the valley. In the afternoon, we’ll visit the archaeological complex of Ollantaytambo, an astonishing Inca town that still preserves its original layout. Its huge terraces, temples and fountains will transport you to the era of the great Inca emperors. At the scheduled time, we’ll board the tourist train to Machu Picchu Pueblo (Aguas Calientes).
Along the way, you’ll see lush landscapes, deep canyons and winding rivers. On arrival, our team will meet you and take you to your hotel in Aguas Calientes to rest and prepare for the big experience the next day.

itinerary.title: Machu Picchu Visit – Return to Cusco
itinerary.description:
Early in the morning, after breakfast, we’ll take the bus for an unforgettable ride up to legendary Machu Picchu, the sacred city of the Incas and one of the New 7 Wonders of the World.
You’ll explore this sanctuary with a guide specialized in Machu Picchu, visiting its most iconic spots: the Main Plaza, where sacred ceremonies were held; the enigmatic Royal Quarters; the impressive Temple of the Three Windows, a symbol of the Andean worldview; the Circular Tower; and the famous Intihuatana, the Inca sundial said to channel the energy of the sun and the mountains. After this magical tour, you can enjoy lunch (optional) in Aguas Calientes, with an exquisite Andean menu.
In the afternoon, you’ll return by tourist train to Ollantaytambo and continue by bus or private car to Cusco, arriving in the evening with your soul full of history and unforgettable landscapes.

itinerary.title: Adventure to the Rainbow Mountain or Humantay Lake
itinerary.description:
Today you’ll enjoy an adventure in pure nature—choose one of these two incredible excursions: Rainbow Mountain (Vinicunca): a high-altitude hike to one of Peru’s most striking landscapes, famous for its natural bands of color that look as if they were painted by the sky. A true geological and spiritual spectacle at more than 5,000 m (16,400 ft) above sea level. Or Humantay Lake: a hike to a turquoise lake nestled at the foot of a snow-capped peak. Surrounded by mountains, this hidden gem is perfect for anyone seeking dreamlike scenery and a connection with nature.
Both options include transportation, breakfast, lunch (drinks not included), entrance fees and a specialized guide. Return to Cusco at approximately 5:30 p.m. Transfer to your hotel and time to rest.

After breakfast, at the agreed time, we’ll transfer you to Cusco airport or the bus station, staying with you until the very last moment to ensure a smooth and pleasant experience.

In the afternoon, you’ll enjoy an unforgettable cultural experience on our Heritage City Tour. You’ll discover the imposing Santa Catalina Monastery, a city within the city that has kept its secrets and traditions for more than 400 years. We’ll walk along streets built of sillar, the white volcanic stone that gave Arequipa its nickname: the White City.
Let yourself be won over by its colonial architecture, centuries-old churches and an atmosphere that breathes elegance and tradition.
Did you know that Arequipa’s historic center is a UNESCO World Heritage Site? And you’re about to experience it firsthand!
🛏️ Overnight in Arequipa.

itinerary.title: Off to Colca: volcanoes, vicuñas and hot springs
itinerary.description:
Start the day with a delicious breakfast, because what awaits is a scenic route that will take your breath away.
Aboard our tourist vehicle, we set off for Chivay, crossing landscapes straight out of a postcard: the Salinas y Aguada Blanca National Reserve, home to free-roaming vicuñas, green fields and mirror-like lagoons. You’ll feel the change in altitude and scenery as we climb to 4,800 m (15,750 ft) above sea level at the Volcanoes Viewpoint, where Misti, Chachani and Ampato greet you with commanding views.
After checking in to your hotel in Chivay, we invite you to relax in the La Calera hot springs, a true natural gift with temperatures reaching 38°C (100°F). Can you imagine soaking in these waters as evening falls over the mountains?
In the evening, you can enjoy dinner with a local folk show, where music, traditional costumes and dances will connect you even more deeply with Colca’s living culture.
🛏️ Overnight in Chivay.

itinerary.title: The condor flight and the heart of Colca

On the way back, we’ll visit traditional villages such as Yanque, Maca and Pinchollo, each with its colonial church, ancestral customs and local markets. We’ll also stop at viewpoints such as Choquetico and Antahuilque, where you can see pre-Inca tombs, ancient farming terraces and the full splendor of the valley.
Return to Arequipa, arrival and transfer to your hotel.

itinerary.title: Arequipa City Tour – Yanahuara Viewpoint – Santa Catalina Monastery
itinerary.description: The tour begins with a visit to the Santa Catalina Monastery, a cloistered citadel founded in the 16th century that is a living catalog of Spanish colonial architecture. After exploring its lanes and cloisters, the group heads to the Plaza de Armas to see the façade of the Cathedral and the Church of La Compañía de Jesús, notable for its mestizo Baroque style and the polychrome dome of the Chapel of San Ignacio. In Yanahuara, we visit the famous viewpoint with its sillar-stone arches inscribed with quotes about the city and direct views of El Misti volcano. itinerary.title: Puno – Uros Floating Islands – Llachón Community
itinerary.description:
At 8:00 a.m. we pick you up from your hotel to begin a magical journey across legendary Lake Titicaca. We travel by private boat to the Uros Titino Islands, floating cultural gems handmade from totora, an ancestral reed that supports both their homes and their traditions. Here you’ll meet the descendants of the Uros people, who still live on the water just as their ancestors did.
We then continue to Llachón, a Quechua community that seems suspended in time. Its people, proud of their Quechua heritage, welcome us in traditional dress and with a warmth that will make you feel at home. You’ll stay in an authentic family home and experience Andean hospitality like never before.
After lunch, you’ll watch a traditional textile demonstration that reveals the symbolism and ancestral wisdom woven into each piece. In the afternoon, you can choose between kayaking on Lake Titicaca, walking along the sacred trails or a sunset sailboat ride.
At nightfall, we’ll share a home-cooked dinner by a bonfire, under one of the starriest skies on the planet. The stories you’ll hear here… will stay with you for a lifetime.

Here you’ll learn about organic farming, the use of traditional medicinal plants and the region’s agricultural customs.
After lunch with your host family, we say goodbye to Llachón and return by boat to Puno, where we drop you off at your hotel to rest.

In the afternoon, at 1:15 p.m., your private City Tour begins, exploring the most iconic sites of colonial and Inca Cusco: the elegant Plaza de Armas, surrounded by colonial architecture and local life; the imposing Cusco Cathedral, a masterpiece of Andean Baroque; and the enigmatic Temple of the Sun – Qoricancha, the most important spiritual center of the Inca world.
You’ll then continue outside the city to visit the most important Inca ruins around Cusco:

You’ll visit the traditional town of Pisac, famous for its craft market, where you can see the customs and textile art of the Andean communities up close.
Crossing the fertile valleys of Calca and Urubamba, you’ll stop for a gourmet buffet lunch made with fresh produce from the valley. You’ll then continue to the imposing archaeological complex of Ollantaytambo, with its terraces, temples and ceremonial channels. This agricultural, military and religious center played a key role in the Inca resistance against the Spanish conquistadors.
At the agreed time, you’ll board a tourist train (Inca Rail or PeruRail) with panoramic windows to Machu Picchu Pueblo (Aguas Calientes). On arrival, you’ll be met and transferred to your hotel.

During the private visit, you’ll explore the main archaeological sectors of this Andean jewel: the Main Plaza, heart of the sacred city; the Royal Quarters, elite residences with stunning views; the Temple of the Three Windows, a reflection of the Inca worldview; the Circular Tower, linked to solar observations; and the enigmatic Intihuatana, or ceremonial sundial.

In the afternoon, you’ll take the tourist train (Inca Rail or PeruRail) to Ollantaytambo, where a private vehicle will be waiting to take you back to your hotel in Cusco.

We’ll continue to the enigmatic Temple of the Sun, or Qoricancha, considered the most important spiritual center of the Andean world, where Inca walls intertwine with the colonial architecture of the Convent of Santo Domingo.
We’ll then leave the city to visit the impressive Inca ruins nearby: Sacsayhuamán, a ceremonial fortress that defies modern logic with the perfection of its colossal stone blocks—some more than 9 m tall and weighing over 350 tons, fitted together without any mortar; Qenqo, an ancient sanctuary carved into the rock that holds the mysteries of ancestral rituals; Puca Pucara, known as the “red fortress,” a strategic military checkpoint and resting place; and Tambomachay, the “Inca’s Bath,” a ceremonial site linked to the worship of water and spiritual purification.
At the end of the tour, we’ll return to your hotel so you can rest and prepare for the most anticipated day of the trip.

We’ll head to the train station, either in Cusco or Ollantaytambo, depending on the route and type of service booked. During the train ride, we’ll pass through spectacular scenery: green valleys, sacred mountains and the mighty Urubamba River. Once in the town of Aguas Calientes, our staff will help you board the tourist buses that will take us on an exciting climb up to the legendary Machu Picchu citadel.
We’ll discover enigmatic Machu Picchu, recognized as “One of the New 7 Wonders of the World,” an ancient legacy that amazes with its architecture, its energy and its connection with the cosmos. During the guided visit (private service), we’ll explore: the Main Plaza, the central hub of ceremonial activities; the Royal Quarters, which show the sophisticated architectural design of the Inca nobility; the Temple of the Three Windows, astronomically aligned with the solstices; the enigmatic Circular Tower, linked to astronomical observations; and the Intihuatana, or sundial, considered an energy and ceremonial center of great importance.

We’ll start at Cusco’s Plaza de Armas, where you can admire the majesty of Cusco Cathedral. Here you can explore an Inca fortress known for its imposing farming terraces and its Temple of the Sun, and learn about its strategic importance in the defense of the empire.
In the afternoon, you’ll take the tourist train to Machu Picchu Pueblo (Aguas Calientes). Along the way, the scenery will take your breath away as Andean valleys and mountains unfold before you. On arrival, our team will help you settle into your hotel and enjoy the peaceful surroundings of this picturesque town.

itinerary.title: Machu Picchu – Return to Cusco

Start your day with pickup at your hotel in Arequipa at 7:00 a.m. and hop aboard our very comfortable private tourist vehicle. You’re about to set off on a fascinating journey to two of Arequipa’s most magical corners: the Pillones Waterfalls and the Stone Forest.
This tour immerses you in the heart of Andean nature, where vivid greenery, mystical rock formations and crystal-clear waters invite you to unplug and enjoy a day full of wonder.
9:00 a.m. Arrival at the Pillones Waterfalls: A hidden paradise
Our first destination is the Pillones Waterfalls, an impressive series of cascades in Arequipa surrounded by lush vegetation. The sound of water falling from above, the fresh highland air and the vibrant energy of this place will make you feel you’ve reached the heart of nature.
Connect with nature: Enjoy the walk to the falls, surrounded by the majesty of the natural setting. The vibrant green of the trees and the crystal-clear water will give you a unique sense of peace and connection.
Incredible photos: The panoramic views of the falls are perfect for capturing epic moments. Don’t forget your camera and get ready for a spectacular moment!
A refreshing dip: If you dare, we invite you to enjoy the cool waters of the falls. Immerse yourself in Arequipa’s natural paradise and feel the energy of Mother Nature.

itinerary.title: 11:30 a.m. Imata Stone Forest: A place full of mystery
itinerary.description:
After admiring the waterfalls, we head to the Imata Stone Forest, a mysterious, magical place that seems straight out of a fairy tale. Here, huge rock formations of volcanic origin rise majestically over the landscape, creating a surreal and striking atmosphere. Unlike anywhere else, this stone forest in Arequipa offers one of the most amazing experiences in the region.
A walk among stone giants: Walk among the rock giants and marvel at their unique shapes. This is a place that invites exploration, discovering every corner and photographing some of Peru’s most impressive landscapes.
Learn its history: As you explore this fascinating forest, our expert Arequipa guides will share local stories and ancient legends about the rock formations and the cultural meaning of this mysterious place.
A place to unplug: The silence of the Imata Stone Forest is broken only by the natural sounds of the wind and the earth, offering the perfect place to relax, breathe deeply and reconnect with yourself.

itinerary.title: 1:00 p.m. Lunch at a local restaurant: Flavors of the Arequipa highlands
itinerary.description:
After a morning full of adventure, it’s time to recharge. We’ll enjoy a delicious traditional lunch, where you can taste the region’s most traditional flavors. From rocoto relleno (stuffed hot pepper) to adobo arequipeño (marinated pork stew), every bite takes you on a culinary journey through Arequipa’s history and culture.
Authentic Arequipa cuisine: With every dish, you’ll feel that the soul of Arequipa is on your table. Best of all, it all comes with the most impressive views of the Peruvian Andes.

itinerary.title: 2:30 p.m. Return to the Pillones Waterfalls: Relax and enjoy
itinerary.description: In the afternoon, we’ll return to the Pillones Waterfalls for one last stop, where you’ll have some free time to explore further or simply relax while taking in the majestic landscape. It’s the perfect moment to reflect, breathe fresh air and soak up the tranquility of nature.

itinerary.title: 4:00 p.m. Return to Arequipa: Unforgettable memories
itinerary.description: Finally, we begin our return to Arequipa, the White City, where you’ll arrive with a heart full of memories and the most amazing photos of this wonderful adventure. This Arequipa tour isn’t just a trip—it’s an experience that connects you with the very essence of Peruvian nature.

description: This service takes care of everything you need to visit the Machu Picchu citadel in a single day, making the most of travel time from Cusco. The itinerary is designed to give you an in-depth look at Inca urban planning and engineering, combining road and rail transport with panoramic-class train service. The day begins at 4:00 a.m. with pickup and transfer to the relevant train station (Poroy or Ollantaytambo). On the road-and-rail route, the drive connects Cusco with the Sacred Valley, where you board the train.
The train travels 112 km along the Urubamba River, passing through different ecological zones down to the ceja de selva (cloud forest at the edge of the jungle). Depending on the class chosen (Vistadome or The 360°), the carriages have glass panels that make it easy to take in the geography and the changing Andean landscape.
On arrival in Aguas Calientes, you transfer to the shuttle bus that takes you to the citadel entrance in 25 minutes. Once at the archaeological site, the guided tour of about 2 hours and 30 minutes begins. Led by an official guide, you’ll explore key structures such as the Guardhouse (a panoramic lookout), the Temple of the Sun, the Sacred Plaza and the system of farming terraces. The explanation focuses on the site’s architectural precision, astronomical alignment and water management.
After the guided tour, you head back down to the town of Aguas Calientes. There is time for lunch and a visit to the local market before boarding the return train. The service ends with a private transfer from the final station to your accommodation in Cusco at approximately 7:00 p.m.

itinerary.description:
The day begins at 8:00 a.m. with pickup from your accommodation. We drive to the Maras plateau, an area known for its farming and its views of the Vilcanota and Vilcabamba mountain ranges.
The first visit is to the Maras Salt Mines. This complex has more than 3,000 evaporation pools fed by an underground spring of hypersaline water. During the tour, your guide explains the crystallization process and the community organization that allows the salt to be harvested in the traditional way. The site is one of the few examples of a pre-Hispanic industry still in operation today.
Next, the group travels to the Moray complex. This archaeological site features natural depressions that were transformed into circular terraces. The layout of these terraces creates microclimates with significant temperature differences between levels, which allowed the Incas to acclimatize a wide range of crops. It is considered an agricultural research center of great architectural precision.
After the guided visits to both sites, we return to Cusco. The service ends at approximately 2:30 p.m. near the Plaza de Armas, close to restaurants and with the afternoon free for your own activities.

description: This tour of the southern part of the Cusco region traces the architectural and artistic evolution of Andean Peru through three key periods: the height of Inca hydraulic engineering, the pre-Inca urban planning of the Wari culture and the religious art of the colonial era. The itinerary is designed for travelers who want to understand the territorial organization and cultural expressions that defined this part of the valley, combining visits to technically remarkable archaeological complexes with historic colonial monuments.

itinerary.description:
The service begins at 8:00 a.m. with pickup from your hotel. We head southeast of the city, through a stretch of the valley known for its farming and varied geography.
Stop 1: Tipón. Located 25 km from Cusco, this site is renowned as a laboratory of hydraulic engineering. During the visit, you’ll see twelve farming terraces with dressed-stone walls and a system of irrigation channels that still work today. The tour includes explanations of areas such as the Intihuatana, the royal compound and the defensive structures that linked this site to the Qhapaq Ñan (the Inca road network).
Stop 2: Pikillaqta. Next, the group travels to this important administrative center of the Wari culture. Covering more than 50 hectares, Pikillaqta stands out for its grid-like urban layout, with narrow streets and two-story buildings made of stone and mud. Exploring this site helps you understand the social and military organization that preceded the expansion of the Inca Empire.
Stop 3: Andahuaylillas. The last stop is the town of Andahuaylillas to visit the Church of San Pedro. This 17th-century church is a key example of Andean Baroque art. Inside, you’ll see frescoes from the Cusco School, coffered ceilings with Mudéjar (Moorish-inspired) influence and altarpieces covered in gold leaf. The visit reveals the cultural fusion expressed in the religious iconography of the colonial period.
The return to Cusco is scheduled for 1:00 p.m., ending near the historic center.

description: The trek to Vinicunca (Rainbow Mountain) is one of the most demanding and visually striking routes in the Cusco region. The mountain stands out for its distinctive sedimentary layers, made up of minerals that display a range of natural colors across the Vilcanota mountain range. The hike requires excellent physical condition because of the altitude and offers a close-up view of the Andean ecosystem, including local wildlife and the surrounding glaciers. It’s a route designed for travelers interested in geology and high-altitude hiking.

itinerary.description:
The day begins at 4:30 a.m. with pickup from your hotel. We drive south in a tourist vehicle—about 2.5 hours—to the community of Tintinco, where breakfast is served to fuel the hike ahead.
We then continue for another hour to Llacto, the trailhead. The climb takes an average of 1 hour and 40 minutes, depending on the group’s pace and the weather. Along the way, you’ll follow a high-mountain trail inhabited by South American camelids, with constant views of the region’s snow-capped peaks.
At the summit, at 5,200 m (17,060 ft) above sea level, you’ll see the geological formation of Vinicunca. Its bands of mineral sediments, exposed by erosion, have earned the site international recognition as one of Peru’s most important geological attractions.
After time to take in the scenery, we descend by the same trail to Llacto to board our vehicle. We make a final stop in Tintinco for a buffet lunch before the service ends in central Cusco (Plaza del Regocijo) at around 4:30 p.m.

description: This high-mountain tour takes you to Humantay Lake, a glacial lake at the foot of the snow-capped peak of the same name in the Andes. recommendations: For a safe experience on high-mountain routes, you’ll need technical clothing in layers (thermal, insulating and waterproof) and hiking boots with ankle support and grippy soles. You should also acclimatize in Cusco for at least 48 hours beforehand and avoid alcohol and heavy meals before the climb to minimize the effects of altitude and stay in top physical shape on the trail.

Broad-spectrum sunscreen, UV-filter sunglasses and wide-brimmed hats are essential because of the intense solar radiation in the mountains. We also recommend staying well hydrated, bringing energy-dense snacks and using trekking poles for better stability on slopes. Finally, carry cash in local currency to pay for extra services run by the communities, such as restrooms or renting additional transport.
important: Departure: Leaving on time is critical for the success of the tour.

faqs.question: What clothing and gear should I bring?

faqs.question: Are there any risks from the altitude?

itinerary.title: Arrival in Lima – South America’s culinary capital – City Tour
itinerary.description:
When you arrive in Lima, our staff will meet you at the airport with personalized assistance and the first “Welcome to Peru!” of your adventure.
After the transfer to your hotel, you’ll have free time to relax or, if you feel like it, join an optional city tour of Lima’s historic center. Discover the Plaza de Armas, the Convent of San Francisco and its catacombs, or admire the sunset from the Miraflores clifftop boardwalk overlooking the Pacific Ocean.
For those who want to start tasting right away, Lima is also known as the culinary capital of the Americas, so we recommend an optional dinner at one of its award-winning restaurants.
🛏 Overnight in Lima.

itinerary.title: Lima / Cusco – Cradle of the Incas and its amazing ruins
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the hotel. At the scheduled time, transfer to the airport for your flight to Cusco, a city where every stone breathes Inca history.
On arrival, we’ll meet you and take you to your hotel. You’ll have time to acclimatize and enjoy a comforting cup of coca tea, an ancient Andean tradition that helps you adjust to the 3,400 m (11,150 ft) altitude.
In the afternoon, we’ll begin a fascinating city tour of Cusco, the former capital of the Inca Empire. We’ll walk through the Plaza de Armas, surrounded by colonial buildings, enter the majestic Cusco Cathedral and visit the Qoricancha, or Temple of the Sun, where the grandeur of the ancient Tawantinsuyu (the Inca Empire) can still be felt.
We’ll then head just outside the city to explore impressive archaeological sites:
🔹 Sacsayhuamán, the Inca ceremonial fortress of colossal stones, some more than 9 m tall and weighing 350 tons.
🔹 Qenqo, with its altar carved into the living rock.
🔹 Puca Pucara, with its defensive role.
🔹 And Tambomachay, known as the “Inca’s Bath,” a sacred site for water worship.
Optionally, you can enjoy a Welcome Dinner at one of Cusco’s best restaurants, with traditional dishes such as cuy chactado (fried guinea pig), lomo saltado (stir-fried beef) or Andean trout with quinoa.
🛏 Overnight in Cusco.

itinerary.title: Cusco / Sacred Valley and on to Machu Picchu Pueblo
itinerary.description:
After breakfast, we head to the Sacred Valley of the Incas, surrounded by Andean mountains, sacred rivers and living traditions.
Our first stop is Pisac, where you’ll explore its colorful craft market full of textiles, ceramics and local products, while villagers in traditional Andean dress still trade as their ancestors did.
We continue through the towns of Calca and Urubamba, where we’ll enjoy a buffet lunch with regional delicacies such as ají de gallina (creamy chili chicken), papa a la huancaína (potatoes in a spicy cheese sauce), Andean salads, tamales and more.
In the afternoon, we reach Ollantaytambo, an Inca archaeological site that combined military, agricultural and religious functions. We’ll climb its Inca terraces to see the ceremonial center, the Temple of the Sun and its system of water channels.
From its station, we’ll board the tourist train to Machu Picchu, which will take us through spectacular scenery to the town of Aguas Calientes (Machu Picchu Pueblo). On arrival, our staff will be waiting to help you check in.
🛏 Overnight in Machu Picchu Pueblo.

itinerary.title: Machu Picchu – Wonder of the World
itinerary.description:
The most anticipated day has arrived! After a delicious breakfast, we’ll take the bus up to the legendary Inca citadel of Machu Picchu, one of the New Seven Wonders of the World.
During the guided visit, you’ll explore the most iconic spots of this masterpiece of Inca architecture:
🔹 The Main Plaza, the heart of the complex.
🔹 The Temple of the Sun, dedicated to the sun.
🔹 The Temple of the Three Windows, which represents the Inca worldview.
🔹 The Tower, possibly used as an astronomical observatory.
🔹 And many more structures connected by Inca stairways, fountains and gardens built with pinpoint precision.
Optional: After the visit, you can enjoy a buffet lunch in Aguas Calientes before taking the train back to Ollantaytambo and continuing by road to Cusco. We’ll arrive in the evening, thrilled and with full hearts.
🛏 Overnight in Cusco.

itinerary.title: Arrival in Lima – Welcome to Peru
itinerary.description:
When you arrive in Lima, Peru’s capital and the former colonial jewel of the Pacific, our team will give you a warm welcome at the airport. Our staff will be waiting with a personalized sign bearing your names to assist you and accompany you on your transfer to the hotel.
🛏️ Overnight in Lima.

itinerary.title: Colonial City Tour of Lima + Food Tour – History, culture and Peruvian flavors
itinerary.description:
After breakfast, we begin a fascinating private tour of Lima’s Historic Center, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. We’ll walk through the imposing Plaza Mayor, admiring architectural gems such as the Government Palace, the Cathedral Basilica, the Archbishop’s Palace and the Municipal Palace, all framed by traditional carved wooden balconies that take us back to the splendor of the viceroyalty.
We’ll visit the Convent and Church of San Francisco, famous for its underground catacombs and magnificent library—one of the most important colonial complexes in the Americas. We’ll then continue to modern Lima to explore the elegant districts of San Isidro and Miraflores. In San Isidro, we’ll stop at the charming El Olivar Park, and in Miraflores we’ll admire the ancient Huaca Pucllana, a pre-Inca ceremonial center surrounded by today’s city.
Next, we’ll enjoy an authentic Lima food experience at a local market in Miraflores. There we’ll discover the ingredients that bring Peru’s acclaimed cuisine to life, taste exotic fruits and uncover unique aromas and flavors. As the perfect finale, we recommend lunch at one of the area’s renowned restaurants (optional).
🛏️ Overnight in Lima.

itinerary.title: Lima / Cusco + Cusco City Tour and Inca ruins
itinerary.description:
Breakfast. Transfer to the airport for your flight to Cusco, the legendary capital of the ancient Inca Empire.
On arrival, you’ll be met and transferred to your hotel to acclimatize to the altitude.
In the afternoon, we’ll begin the Cusco City Tour: we’ll visit the iconic Plaza de Armas, surrounded by colonial churches built on top of ancient Inca palaces.
We’ll enter the majestic Cathedral and then the Temple of the Sun, or Qoricancha, the most sacred site of the Tawantinsuyu (the Inca Empire), which today stands alongside the colonial architecture of the Convent of Santo Domingo.
We’ll leave the city to explore the nearby Inca archaeological sites:
Sacsayhuamán, an imposing ceremonial fortress of colossal stones fitted together with pinpoint precision; Qenqo, an ancient temple carved into the living rock; Puca Pucara, a military checkpoint with panoramic views; and Tambomachay, a ceremonial site linked to water and fertility.
🛏️ Return to the hotel and overnight in Cusco.

itinerary.title: Sacred Valley of the Incas + Ollantaytambo + Aguas Calientes
itinerary.description:
After breakfast, we’ll set off for the enchanting Sacred Valley of the Incas, a fertile valley full of living culture, colorful Andean markets and breathtaking landscapes.
Our first stop will be the town of Pisac, where we’ll explore its craft market, famous for Andean textiles, ceramics and jewelry—the perfect place to shop for traditional Peruvian souvenirs. We continue through the towns of Calca and Urubamba, where we’ll enjoy a buffet lunch with fresh regional produce.
Further on, we reach Ollantaytambo, an amazing living Inca town with an archaeological complex of farming terraces, temples and ritual fountains. Its fortress, built into the mountainside, played a key role in the defense of the empire.
In the late afternoon, we’ll board a panoramic train to Machu Picchu (Inca Rail or PeruRail), which will take us through jungle-clad scenery to the town of Aguas Calientes at the foot of Machu Picchu. On arrival, assistance from the train station to your hotel.
🛏️ Overnight in Aguas Calientes.

itinerary.title: Machu Picchu – The Lost City of the Incas
itinerary.description:
Very early, after breakfast, we’ll board the bus that climbs the mountain to the enigmatic citadel of Machu Picchu, one of the New Seven Wonders of the World.
During the guided tour of Machu Picchu (private), we’ll discover its main structures: the Main Plaza, the Royal Quarters, the Temple of the Three Windows, the Circular Tower and the Intihuatana sundial, a key point of spiritual energy.
After the visit, you can enjoy a buffet lunch in Aguas Calientes (optional). We’ll then return by train to Ollantaytambo and continue by shared or private vehicle to Cusco.
🛏️ Overnight in Cusco.

itinerary.title: Route of the Sun – Cusco to Puno
itinerary.description:
After breakfast, we’ll begin the journey by tourist bus from Cusco to Puno along the legendary Route of the Sun (Ruta del Sol), a trip full of culture, history and Andean scenery.
We’ll visit: Andahuaylillas, with its famous Church of San Pedro Apóstol, known as the “Sistine Chapel of the Americas” for its stunning frescoes.
The archaeological complex of Raqchi, dedicated to the god Wiracocha.
Sicuani, where we’ll enjoy an Andean buffet lunch. The Abra La Raya mountain pass (4,335 m (14,220 ft) above sea level), the highest point of the route. The Pukara Lithic Museum, which houses remains of a pre-Inca civilization. We’ll arrive in Puno at sunset.
🛏️ Overnight in Puno.

itinerary.title: Lake Titicaca – Uros Floating Islands and Taquile Island
itinerary.description:
After breakfast, we’ll set off across legendary Lake Titicaca, the highest navigable lake in the world.
Our first stop will be the Uros Floating Islands, built entirely of totora, an aquatic reed that grows in the lake. These floating islands have been home to an ancient people who, more than 500 years ago, chose to live on the water to protect themselves from other cultures. Today, they still preserve their traditional way of life.
We continue to Taquile Island, famous for its traditional textiles, recognized by UNESCO as Intangible Cultural Heritage. Its Quechua inhabitants maintain a communal organization and ancestral customs. We’ll have lunch on the island with local produce and walk along its archaeological trails.
In the afternoon, we’ll return to Puno.
🛏️ Overnight in Puno.

recommendations: Luggage: Use one large suitcase for the whole trip, but keep a 20-liter backpack handy. You’ll use it for the overnight stay on Amantaní (Day 8) and at Machu Picchu (Day 12), since heavy luggage isn’t allowed in those areas.
Thermal protection: The temperature range is extreme. In Ica it may be 28°C (82°F), while in Colca or Puno it can drop to -5°C (23°F) at night. Bring good-quality thermal clothing.
Health and altitude: Start the trip by drinking plenty of water in Lima. When you reach Arequipa (Day 4), your body will begin to acclimatize. Don’t ignore headaches—coca tea is your best ally.
Money: Although Cusco and Lima are modern cities, only cash (soles) is accepted on Amantaní and in the Colca villages.
Technology: Bring a portable charger (power bank). Electricity on Amantaní Island is limited and solar-powered.
important: Altitude management: This itinerary is cleverly designed—it starts at sea level and climbs gradually (Arequipa → Colca → Puno → Cusco), which dramatically reduces the risk of altitude sickness (soroche).
Luggage on the train: For the night in Aguas Calientes (Day 12), the train only allows a 5 kg backpack. Your main luggage will be stored at your hotel in Cusco.
The Amantaní experience: On Day 8 you’ll stay with a local family. Facilities are basic but cozy and clean, offering the most authentic cultural immersion of the trip.
Nazca – Arequipa: The Day 3 drive is the longest overland leg. We recommend getting a good night’s rest beforehand.

itinerary.title: Welcome to Lima – The City of Kings
itinerary.description:
Your adventure begins! When you arrive in Peru’s capital, our team will meet you at the airport with a warm, personalized welcome. We’ll take you comfortably to your hotel while giving you a brief introduction to this vibrant city.
Lima, known as the City of Kings, is a fascinating crossroads of colonial past and cosmopolitan present. You’ll have the afternoon free to rest or explore the surrounding area on your own.
🛏 Overnight in Lima.

itinerary.title: Colonial and Modern Lima and the Flavors of Peru
itinerary.description:
After breakfast, get ready for a private tour of Lima full of history, architecture and unique flavors. We’ll start in Lima’s Historic Center, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
You’ll walk through elegant Plaza San Martín and the imposing Plaza Mayor, surrounded by buildings such as the Government Palace, Lima Cathedral and the Municipal Palace, all with elegant colonial balconies. We’ll also go inside the Convent of San Francisco, famous for its Baroque art and underground catacombs.
Next, we’ll head to modern Lima, touring the elegant districts of San Isidro and Miraflores. You’ll see the peaceful El Olivar Park, with its centuries of history, and the ancient Huaca Pucllana, a pre-Inca ceremonial center in the middle of the city.
Later, you’ll enjoy a cultural and sensory experience at a traditional market in Miraflores, where you’ll learn about the ingredients behind Peru’s celebrated cuisine. You’ll taste exotic Peruvian fruits such as cherimoya, lúcuma and camu camu while we introduce you to the secrets of Peruvian cooking. Optional: End the tour with a gourmet lunch at one of Lima’s best restaurants, featuring signature dishes such as ceviche, anticuchos (grilled skewers) or ají de gallina (creamy chili chicken).
🛏 Overnight in Lima.

itinerary.title: Lima / Cusco – Living history among the mountains
itinerary.description:
After breakfast, we’ll take the flight to Cusco, the former capital of the Inca Empire. Our staff will meet you at the airport and take you to your hotel, where you can rest and acclimatize while enjoying a traditional cup of coca tea.
In the afternoon, we’ll begin a fascinating city tour of Cusco. You’ll stroll through the charming Plaza de Armas, lined with colonial arcades, and visit the Cathedral and the legendary Qoricancha, or Temple of the Sun, once one of the most sacred places in the Andean world.
We’ll then head out to explore Cusco’s archaeological sites:
🔹 Sacsayhuamán, with its colossal walls of perfectly fitted stones.
🔹 Qenqo, a mysterious ceremonial center.
🔹 Puca Pucara, which guarded access to the city.
🔹 And Tambomachay, dedicated to the worship of water.
A perfect day to connect with the greatness of the Andean past.
🛏 Overnight in Cusco.

itinerary.title: Sacred Valley Tour / Aguas Calientes
itinerary.description:
Early breakfast and departure for the magical Sacred Valley of the Incas, a place where time seems to stand still. We’ll visit Pisac, known for its craft market, where you’ll see how ancestral weaving, pottery and metalworking techniques are kept alive. It’s a great chance to buy authentic, one-of-a-kind souvenirs.
We continue through the towns of Calca and Urubamba, where we’ll stop for an Andean buffet lunch surrounded by mountains. The route continues to Ollantaytambo, an Inca archaeological complex built on terraces. We’ll climb to the top to discover a water temple, ceremonial channels and structures that guarded the entrance to the Sacred Valley.
From Ollantaytambo station, we’ll take the tourist train to Machu Picchu (Inca Rail or PeruRail) to the town of Aguas Calientes, as the scenery shifts between mountains, rivers and cloud forest. On arrival, assistance at the station and transfer to your hotel.
🛏 Overnight in Aguas Calientes.

itinerary.title: Machu Picchu – A life-changing wonder / Cusco
itinerary.description:
After breakfast, we take the bus up to the iconic citadel of Machu Picchu, the jewel of the Inca world and a Wonder of the Modern World.
During your guided visit to Machu Picchu (private), you’ll explore:
🔹 The Main Plaza, the ceremonial core.
🔹 The Royal Quarters, where the Inca elite lived.
🔹 The Temple of the Three Windows, a symbol of the Andean trilogy (the three realms of the Andean worldview).
🔹 The Circular Tower, possibly a solar observatory.
🔹 And Machu Picchu’s stunning natural setting, which gives off a special energy.
Optional: After the tour, you can enjoy a buffet lunch in Aguas Calientes, with traditional dishes fused with international cuisine. In the afternoon, we’ll board the tourist train back toward Cusco, connecting by road from there.
🛏 Overnight in Cusco.

itinerary.title: Return to Lima / The end of an unforgettable experience

After breakfast, at the scheduled time, we’ll take you to the airport for your flight back to Lima, where this unforgettable adventure through Peru comes to an end.

itinerary.title: Lima – Juliaca – Sillustani Archaeological Complex
itinerary.description:
When you arrive at Juliaca airport, we’ll welcome you with the typical warmth of the Peruvian Altiplano and head straight to one of the region’s most enigmatic sites: the Sillustani archaeological complex.
Set on the shores of Lake Umayo, this pre-Inca site will amaze you with its chullpas, impressive funerary towers built by the Kolla culture between the 12th and 14th centuries. These cylindrical structures, some up to 12 m tall, were raised as a necropolis for great dignitaries. Their unusual architecture, with a base narrower than the top, still puzzles many modern engineers.
As you explore this mystical place, surrounded by breathtaking scenery, you’ll feel time stand still amid the Altiplano winds and the calm waters of the lake.
After the visit, we’ll continue to your hotel in Puno, where you can rest and acclimatize.

itinerary.title: Lake Titicaca Boat Trip – Uros Floating Islands and Taquile
itinerary.description:
Today you’ll enjoy one of the most authentic and unforgettable experiences in southern Peru. After breakfast, we’ll leave at 7:00 a.m. for the port of Puno, where we’ll board a boat to cross the sacred waters of Lake Titicaca, the highest navigable lake in the world.
After 40 minutes on the water, we’ll reach the Uros Floating Islands, a group of platforms made entirely of totora, a reed that grows in the lake. You’ll see how this ancient people has built houses, boats and even schools on these floating islands for more than 500 years to escape Inca and Kolla rule. You’ll hear their stories, learn about their customs and, if you wish, ride one of their famous totora reed boats.
The adventure continues to Taquile Island, whose Quechua inhabitants proudly preserve their culture and age-old traditions. This community is world-renowned for its handwoven textiles, considered by UNESCO to be among the finest on the planet.
Here we’ll enjoy a traditional Andean lunch with views of the majestic lake and walk along trails lined with farming terraces and archaeological remains, while learning about the island’s community system, considered one of the most sustainable in the Altiplano. In the afternoon, we’ll return by boat to Puno, where you’ll have free time to rest or explore the city on your own. Overnight at your selected hotel.

You’ll take with you lasting memories of a destination that brings together pre-Inca history, sublime nature and a living culture that still beats strongly in the heart of Lake Titicaca.

itinerary.title: An ancestral adventure through the hidden landscapes of the southern Andes
itinerary.description:
Bright and early, at 5:00 a.m., we begin one of the most authentic and moving experiences in all of southern Peru. We’ll pick you up from your hotel and head for the province of Canas, home to the most vibrant and astonishing living Inca legacy that still survives: the Q’eswachaka bridge.
After two hours on the road through the golden valleys of southern Cusco, we’ll stop at a local restaurant for a traditional breakfast: fresh bread, freshly brewed coffee, seasonal fruit and plenty of Andean warmth. The perfect way to start the day!

itinerary.title: Hidden lakes and dormant volcanoes
itinerary.description:
The route continues through natural scenery that looks like postcards from another world. We’ll visit the beautiful high Andean lakes of Pampamarca, Asnacqocha, Acopía and Pomacanchi, each with its own legend and reflection of the sky. The road also takes us close to the Pabellones volcano, a sleeping giant that has watched over these lands for centuries.
The Q’eswachaka Bridge: crossing centuries of history in a single step
And finally, we reach the most anticipated moment: Q’eswachaka, a bridge woven from plant fibers suspended over the imposing canyon of the Apurímac River, at more than 3,700 m (12,140 ft). This is no ordinary bridge. It is the only original Inca bridge still in use, rewoven by hand every June by four local communities (Huinchiri, Chaupibanda, Ccollana Quehue and Perccaro) in an ancestral ceremony declared by UNESCO as Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity.
Walking across it is much more than an adventure: it’s crossing a threshold between the present and the living history of the Andes. You’ll feel the wind, the altitude and the spirituality of the place connect you with something bigger.
And don’t worry—it’s completely safe! The annual renewal ensures its strength and resilience using age-old techniques.

itinerary.title: Cusco – Route of the Sun – Puno
itinerary.description:
Very early in the morning, we’ll pick you up and leave Cusco aboard a comfortable tourist bus bound for the mystical city of Puno, traveling one of the most cultural and scenic routes in the country: the Route of the Sun.
Our journey starts at 6:30 a.m. from the bus station. The first stop takes us to the charming town of Andahuaylillas, home to one of the jewels of colonial religious art: the Church of San Pedro Apóstol, also known as the “Sistine Chapel of the Americas.” Its interior, decorated with gilded frescoes, Baroque murals and handcrafted ceilings, is a true hidden treasure in the Andes.
We continue to the archaeological complex of Raqchi, where we’ll discover the remains of the majestic Temple of the god Wiracocha. This sacred site was one of the most important religious centers of the Inca Empire and still preserves remains of cyclopean walls and ritual storehouses that connect us with Andean spiritual thought.
Our next stop is Sicuani, where we’ll enjoy a buffet lunch with regional flavors—perfect for recharging in the middle of this cultural journey. The route continues to the imposing Abra La Raya pass, the highest point of the route at over 4,300 m (14,110 ft) above sea level, where we can enjoy spectacular views of the snow-capped Andes.
Finally, we’ll reach the Pukara Lithic Museum, cradle of one of the oldest civilizations of the Altiplano. Here we’ll see enigmatic monolithic sculptures and learn about the origins of pre-Inca culture.
We’ll end this unique day in Puno (around 5:30 p.m.), where we’ll take you straight to your hotel to rest.

itinerary.title: Lake Titicaca Boat Trip – Uros Islands & Taquile
itinerary.description:
After breakfast, we’ll begin an unforgettable experience on the sacred waters of legendary Lake Titicaca, considered the highest navigable lake on the planet.
At 7:00 a.m., we’ll head to the port of Puno to board a motorboat bound for the amazing Uros Floating Islands. Made entirely of totora reeds, these islands are a true testament to ancestral survival. You’ll meet their inhabitants, descendants of an ancient people who chose to isolate themselves from the world by building their own life on the water.
Next, we’ll continue to Taquile Island, a place where time seems to have stood still. Its Quechua inhabitants have kept their communal organization intact, along with one of the finest hand-weaving traditions in the world, declared Intangible Cultural Heritage by UNESCO.
We’ll enjoy a traditional lunch prepared by a local family, then walk the island’s trails, visiting its hills, farming terraces and archaeological remains.
In the afternoon, we’ll return to Puno. Overnight at your selected hotel.

description: The Sillustani archaeological complex is one of the most important funerary sites in the central Andes. Set on a peninsula overlooking Lake Umayo, it stands out for its imposing chullpas, or funerary towers, built by the Colla culture and later refined by the Incas. The precision of the stonework and the engineering behind these structures—up to 12 m tall—reflect the high status of the people buried there and the complexity of their funeral rites. It’s an essential destination for understanding the architectural evolution and beliefs about the afterlife on the Altiplano.

itinerary.description: The tour begins with pickup from your hotel for a drive of about 45 minutes northwest of Puno. On arrival at the archaeological site, we set off on a gradual uphill walk to explore the different areas of this pre-Inca and Inca cemetery. During the visit, the guide will explain the construction methods, the use of ramps to raise the stone blocks and the meaning of the carvings on the walls. Besides exploring the towers, the itinerary includes a stop at natural viewpoints to observe the wildlife and ecosystem of Lake Umayo. Before returning to Puno, we make a short visit to a local community to see traditional rural homes and their way of life on the Altiplano.

description: The Colca Canyon is one of Peru’s most impressive geological and cultural destinations. Reaching a depth of 4,160 m, it is the natural habitat of the Andean condor (Vultur gryphus), the iconic bird of the Andes. This full-day tour is designed to make the most of your time, letting you watch sunrise over the mountains, spot condors at the Cruz del Cóndor viewpoint and explore the traditional villages of the valley, where the Collagua and Cabana cultures keep their ancestral farming techniques and traditional dress alive.

On the way back to Chivay, we stop at natural viewpoints such as Antahuilque to see the pre-Inca farming terraces and visit the villages of Maca and Yanque, known for their colonial religious architecture. description: This full-day boat trip on Lake Titicaca combines two of the most historically and socially significant destinations in the Puno region. It links the floating Uros Islands, known for their unique way of life on platforms of totora reeds, with Taquile Island, recognized by UNESCO as a Masterpiece of the Oral and Intangible Heritage of Humanity for its textile excellence. The tour is designed to offer an in-depth look at island life and at community structures that have endured in the face of modernity, in a unique setting more than 3,812 m (12,510 ft) above sea level.

On arrival, we take a moderate uphill walk to the village center to learn about the island’s social organization and local textile art, in which men are the main weavers. After a demonstration of the meaning of the designs and the use of natural plants to wash the wool, a traditional lunch is served featuring local produce such as trout and quinoa. The day ends with the walk down to the main dock to board the boat back to Puno, followed by the transfer to your hotel.

The tour offers an in-depth look at how salt flats form, artisanal salt harvesting and hot springs in volcanic areas, ending at the natural pools of Lojen, known for their mineral-rich, therapeutic waters.

Located near the town of Juli, this structure carved into a sandstone rock face is regarded in the Andean worldview as a sacred portal linked to ancient deities. The site is surrounded by natural rock formations that add significant geological interest to the tour. On arrival at Hayu Marca, we’ll walk along the stone paths leading to the main gateway and the adjacent structures. Your specialized guide will explain the carving technique, the monument’s alignment and the oral traditions about the origin of Aramu Muru. After plenty of time for photos and taking in the surroundings, the tour continues to the town of Juli, historically known as the “Rome of the Indies,” to see its colonial architecture from the outside before returning directly to Puno.

The route is designed to explore Inca architecture and urban planning at strategic sites such as Pisac and Ollantaytambo. The itinerary includes seeing the farming terraces, exploring the colonial structures of Chinchero and a lunch stop in Urubamba. itinerary.description:
At 7:45 a.m., our adventure begins with pickup from your accommodation. Aboard our tourist vehicle, we’ll head to the picturesque town of Pisac, home to impressive Inca ruins laid out in the shape of a partridge, built high on a hill with terraces that seem to touch the sky.
Next, we’ll stop at the Taray Viewpoint, where you’ll enjoy an unbeatable panoramic view of the valley, with its fields, towering mountains and the winding Vilcanota River.
In the town of Pisac, you’ll have free time to browse its famous craft market, ideal for buying textiles, silver jewelry and ceramics made by local hands.
We’ll continue to Urubamba, the capital of the valley, where you’ll enjoy an Andean buffet lunch featuring the best of traditional Peruvian cuisine. Recharged, we’ll head to the archaeological complex of Ollantaytambo, a living Inca town and strategic fortress, with terraces, temples and ceremonial channels that reveal the architectural wisdom of the Tawantinsuyu (the Inca Empire).
On the way back to Cusco, we’ll stop in the peaceful town of Chinchero to visit its beautiful colonial church dedicated to Our Lady of Montserrat, built on ancient Inca foundations. Here you can also learn more about the weaving traditions that are still alive today.
We’ll end the tour arriving in Cusco at around 6:30 p.m., full of memories, landscapes and insights that will stay with you forever.

cardSummary: Discover the wonders of Lake Titicaca on a unique tour of the floating Uros Islands, Amantaní Island and Taquile Island. Enjoy an immersive cultural experience, meet ancestral communities and take in stunning scenery in Puno.
description:
Enjoy a unique experience in the heart of Lake Titicaca, the highest navigable lake in the world.
Set off on a fascinating journey to the floating Uros Islands, where past and present meet in a place built entirely of totora reeds. Then let yourself be enchanted by Amantaní Island, home to Quechua communities, and enjoy an indescribable sunset from Cerro Pachamama (Pachamama Hill). Visit mystical Taquile Island, famous for its textile art and the hospitality of its people. A journey full of culture, ancestral traditions and breathtaking scenery awaits you on this exclusive circuit.

Day 2: Visit to Taquile Island and return to Puno.
Day 3: Departure transfer (Puno to Lima or your next destination).

itinerary.title: Puno – Uros Floating Islands – Amantaní Island
itinerary.description:
At 7:00 a.m., we’ll begin our adventure on majestic Lake Titicaca, where a transformative experience awaits. We’ll pick you up from your hotel in Puno and head to the lake port to board a boat to the legendary Uros Floating Islands.
These floating islands, built by hand from totora, a reed that grows in the lake, are a living example of ancestral ingenuity. For an hour and a half, you’ll learn about the history of this ancient people who chose to live on the water, isolating themselves from the Incas and proudly preserving their legacy.
The journey continues for 3 hours across the blue waters of Titicaca to Amantaní Island, a cultural gem inhabited by Quechua communities.
On arrival, a local family will welcome you warmly and serve a home-cooked lunch full of Andean flavor. In the afternoon, we’ll hike together up Cerro Pachamama, the island’s highest point, where you’ll watch a sunset over Titicaca that you’ll simply never forget. In the evening, after a community dinner, you can join a small local celebration: the islanders will invite you to dance in their traditional dress to their own music.

itinerary.title: Amantaní Island – Taquile Island – Puno
itinerary.description:
After an Andean breakfast, we’ll board the boat again for legendary Taquile Island, famous for being home to the best weavers in the world, according to UNESCO.
As you walk the island’s paths, you’ll be struck by the harmony of its communal system, the hospitality of its people and the beauty of its textiles. Here, every woven garment tells a story and represents a vital part of the islanders’ worldview.
We’ll enjoy a traditional lunch at a local home and then head back to Puno, arriving at around 3:00 p.m. We’ll drop you off at your hotel so you can rest with a heart full of memories.

itinerary.title: Puno – Departure Transfer
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the hotel. At the agreed time, we’ll transfer you to the airport or bus terminal to continue your journey or head home, taking with you a deep connection with the living cultures of Titicaca.

description: Enjoy a unique adventure to one of Peru’s best-kept secrets! Leaving early, we’ll head to Waqrapukara, an ancient fortress located at 4,300 m (14,110 ft) above sea level. On a challenging trek surrounded by stunning Andean scenery, you’ll reach this sacred temple and discover its ceremonial plazas and watchtowers. Take in the panoramic views of this site full of history and ancestral energy, and end the day with a delicious traditional lunch before returning to Cusco with unforgettable memories.

itinerary.title: The adventure begins – 4:00 a.m.
itinerary.description: Very early in the morning, just as the first rays of sun begin to touch the mountains, we’ll pick you up at your hotel in Cusco. We’ll set off on a two-hour drive south of the Sacred Valley toward the town of Cusipata, where an Andean buffet breakfast full of local flavors awaits: quinoa, freshly baked bread, fresh fruit and energizing herbal teas.

itinerary.title: Into the unknown
itinerary.description: With full stomachs and high spirits, we continue along a route that seems straight out of a movie: turquoise lakes, adobe villages full of living history and mist-covered valleys that make you feel you’re inside a legend. After another two hours on the road, we reach the trailhead: the small town of Pitumarca.

itinerary.title: Trek to the sacred (8 km)
itinerary.description:
This is where the real challenge begins. We’ll hike for about 3 hours, climbing gradually along ancient paths surrounded by towering mountains and a silence broken only by the wind and the song of high-Andean birds. Along the way, you may see llamas, vicuñas, condors and, if you’re lucky, even Andean foxes.
Every step brings us closer to a sacred place in the Andes, a site that still holds secrets of a glorious past.

itinerary.title: Waqrapukara – The temple in the sky
itinerary.description:
Finally, at 4,300 m (14,110 ft) above sea level, Waqrapukara will appear before you: an archaeological site carved onto the top of an Andean canyon. Its name means “Fortress of Horns,” after the two natural rock formations that guard it like divine watchtowers. During the guided visit, we’ll explore: the Intipunku, or “Sun Gate,” a ceremonial portal where ancient pilgrims greeted the dawn; ceremonial plazas aligned with the stars; watchtowers, shrines and ritual enclosures built by the Quinchas, a pre-Inca people; and panoramic views that will take your breath away… and not just because of the altitude.
Here, we invite you to close your eyes and breathe deeply. Feel the energy of the mountain surround you. This is no ordinary place: it’s a natural altar to the Apus, the guardian spirits of the Andes.

itinerary.title: Return with a full heart
itinerary.description:
After taking in one of Peru’s best-kept secrets, we’ll return along the same trail to Pitumarca, where our transport will be waiting. In Cusipata, we’ll stop for a buffet lunch full of local flavors: traditional stews, fresh salads, Andean herbal teas and traditional sweets.
Finally, at around 6:00 p.m., we’ll arrive in Cusco, where this magical day ends with drop-off at Plaza Regocijo.

recommendations: Wear suitable trekking clothes: Make sure you wear comfortable, breathable clothing suitable for long walks. Bring a light jacket, especially if you’re traveling in the cold season.
Hiking footwear: Comfortable, sturdy shoes for walking on uneven ground are essential.
Sun protection: Don’t forget sunscreen, sunglasses and a hat or cap to protect yourself from UV radiation, especially at high altitude.
Hydration: Bring a reusable water bottle to stay hydrated during the trek.
Warm clothing: Even if the day is warm, temperatures at altitude can drop quickly, so we recommend bringing an extra jacket or sweater.
Camera: Waqrapukara offers stunning views, so don’t forget your camera or phone to capture those unforgettable moments.
Prepare your body for the altitude: If you’re sensitive to altitude, we recommend arriving in Cusco in advance to acclimatize, or asking a doctor about preventive measures.
Respect the site: Remember that Waqrapukara is a sacred site. Follow the site rules and your guide’s instructions, and take care of the environment.
important: Altitude and acclimatization: The route reaches up to 4,300 m (14,110 ft) above sea level. It’s crucial that travelers are well acclimatized before the trek to avoid altitude sickness. We recommend being in Cusco for at least 1–2 days before the tour to adjust better.

Physical preparation: The trek is moderately difficult. Although no previous experience is required, good physical condition is important for the climb of about 3 hours. The trail is uneven and can be demanding because of the thin air at high altitude.
Safety on the route:
During the trek, guides will be on hand to provide assistance and make sure the route is safe. We recommend following the guide’s instructions and staying with the group at all times.
Restrooms: There are no restrooms along the trek, so we suggest using the facilities in Pitumarca before starting the hike or at the Cusipata rest area on the way back.
Wildlife: During the trek, you may see native animals such as llamas, alpacas, vicuñas and even condors and Andean foxes, making for a unique experience of Andean nature.

About the archaeological site: Waqrapukara is an impressive and spiritual archaeological site set on top of a canyon. Visitors will see rock formations, ceremonial plazas, the Intipunku (Sun Gate) and sacred temples, offering a deep connection with Andean culture and spirituality.

faqs.question: How difficult is the trek to Waqrapukara?
faqs.answer: The trek is moderate to challenging because of the altitude (you’ll reach 4,300 m (14,110 ft) above sea level) and its length (about 3 hours of climbing). We recommend being acclimatized to Cusco before the trek and bringing enough water.

faqs.question: Do I need previous trekking experience?
faqs.answer: You don’t need advanced experience, but you do need to be in good physical shape, as the climb can be demanding because of the altitude.

faqs.question: How long does it take to reach Waqrapukara?
faqs.answer: The trek to Waqrapukara takes about 3 hours of climbing. Along the way, you can enjoy spectacular views of mountains, valleys and local wildlife.

faqs.question: Will there be time to rest during the trek?
faqs.answer: Yes, the guide will make regular stops to rest and drink water. It’s important not to rush and to take the time you need to adjust to the altitude.

faqs.question: Can I hire a horse to make the route easier?
